titleStmt.title: Memorandum of Conversation, by Mr. Walter A. Adams, of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs

head.hi: Memorandum of Conversation, by Mr. Walter A. Adams, of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs

row.cell: Mr. Tswen-ling Tsui, First Secretary, Chinese Embassy

div.p:
Mr. Tsui called at his own request and handed Mr. Hamilton the attached translation of a telegram of August 8, 1939, from Dr. H. H. Kung, Chinese Minister of Finance, in which there is solicited the concern of the Government of the United States in regard to the question of certain silver deposits in Tientsin. Mr. Hamilton explained that the attitude of this Government toward the Tientsin situation was perfectly clear: that through statements by the Secretary and in such other ways as seemed to be appropriate and practicable this Government had made clear that, while it was not concerned in certain aspects of the Tientsin situation, it was concerned and interested with regard to the broader issues arising out of and involved in the Tientsin situation, including the question of currency. Mr. Hamilton said that
this Government was desirous of being as helpful as practicable in regard to the currency situation, having in mind all the circumstances involved. He pointed out, however, that with respect to the actual custody and protection of the silver on deposit at Tientsin our position was different from that of the British and French authorities. He said that he understood that the silver was in non-American banks located in the British and French Concessions.
Mr. Tsui said that he understood that this was so and indicated that he also understood the distinction which Mr. Hamilton had made.
It is thought that Mr. Tsui does not expect a further reply to the message under reference.

note.p: See also vol. iii, pp. 348 ff.
